title: Trump teases ‘big, beautiful’ European security deal after meeting Putin envoy | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

US President Donald Trump has promised a new security deal for Ukraine that “might involve all of Europe” after meeting a top Russian envoy on Thursday, but the proposal offers few details and has left European capitals puzzled.

“It’s going to be a big agreement…It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe. It’s going to be a big, beautiful agreement, and everyone’s going to be thrilled,” Trump told reporters on Thursday, without going into any details.

The president, who has promised to secure a deal to end the war in Ukraine on multiple occasions in the past, made the comments after meeting with Kirill Dmitriev, the sanctioned CEO of Russia’s sovereign wealth fund who serves as an envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also on Thursday posted a statement on X, arguing that “a broader European security architecture” was needed to “address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment.”

“For more than 30 years, Europe and Russia have struggled to establish a sustainable security framework. Decades of mistrust, competing security concerns, and the devastating consequences of this war make this an extraordinarily difficult challenge, but one that is essential to lasting peace,” Kushner said in the statement.

Kushner made no mention that it was Russia that invaded Ukraine, nor thespate of hybrid attacksEurope blames on Russia.

Kushner also argued for “greater military transparency, (and) reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks” between Russia and Europe — a remark that might cause alarm in some parts of Europe given Moscow’s long-standing position that NATO’s presence in eastern Europe is in itself an escalation.

He added the US held recent talks with Ukraine, NATO, and other European partners, and said Trump “advanced” a discussion about security with European leaders.

However, several European officials with knowledge of the conflict told CNN they did not know what Trump was referring to.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that he didn’t know many details of the potential new security framework floated by Trump but warned a deal between Russia and Europe would not be simple and could potentially be dangerous.

Speaking to CNN’s Jake Tapper on Friday, Zelensky said that he had become aware of a potential new security framework following a phone call on Thursday withKushner and US special envoy Steve Witkoff to prepare for US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi next week.

“For me, it’s not simple and it can be dangerous,” Zelensky said, adding that discussions to end the war in Ukraine must come first, and security guarantees second.

Trump spoke to the German Chancellor ‌Friedrich Merz on Thursday, a key backer of Ukraine. A German government official refused to speak in detail about the content of the call but said that the new ideas put forward by the Trump administration are based on negotiations in recent months.

It is unclear if Trump spoke to any other European leaders.

Meanwhile, NATO spokesperson Allison Hart confirmed that talks between NATO, the US, Ukraine, and EU and European counterparts took place in Brussels on Thursday, ahead of the of trilateral meeting between the US, Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi next week.

Hart said the meeting “sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine,” but refused to disclose any details.

Dmitriev was at the White House on Thursday for an event organized by first ladyMelania Trump, who brought together representatives of Russia and Ukraine to mark last week’s successful ceasefire in the occupied Ukrainian city ofOleshky.

Speaking to reporters later, Trump said he did not meet the Ukrainian delegation.

Trump has recently renewed his push for a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine after a public spat with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

But despite the promises, the war is still raging, with Russia killing Ukrainian civilians on a daily basis. In one attack earlier this week, Moscow dropped nine bombs on an underground shelter just as people gathered there to collect humanitarian aid. At least53 people were killedin one of the deadliest attacks of a conflict now in its fifth year.

In his daily address on Friday, Zelensky warned that Russia is preparing another attack on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and bridges. “We now have intel that another strike is being prepared — targeting our energy sector, bridges across the Dnipro, and civilian infrastructure,” he said, as he renewed his plea for Patriot interceptor missiles from Ukraine’s allies.

In a post on social media, the Ukrainian leader said Kyiv’s attacks on Russia’s oil refineries are continuing, in response to Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy facilities.

Putin continues to make maximalist demands from Ukraine, including Russian control over the whole of Ukraine’s eastern Donbas region, a reduction in the size of Ukraine’s military and the abandonment of Kyiv’s ambitions to join NATO — red lines that Kyiv says indicate he is not serious about negotiating a peace deal.

CNN’s Nick Paton Walsh and Sebastian Shukla contributed reporting.

CNN’s Nick Paton Walsh and Sebastian Shukla contributed reporting.
